summary: Adversarial multi-method verification of the claimed n=6 CTLN counterexample (graph idx 1387528)

synthesis.summary:
CLAIM: the 6-node, 18-edge digraph X (bidirected pairs {1,5},{2,5},{3,4},{4,5}; one-way edges 0->1, 0->2, 3->0, 4->0, 5->0, 3->1, 1->4, 2->3, 2->4, 5->3; no edge between 1 and 2) supports a stable fixed point of the CTLN with FULL support at the legal parameter points P1 (eps=1/101, delta=27/2626, q=1350/1313) and P2 (eps=1/1001, delta=27/26026, q=13500/13013). Since the full support is not a clique, this contradicts Curto-Morrison Open Question 10 (target-free clique conjecture) inside the open gap 1 < q < n-2.

VERDICT: VERIFIED. Five independent re-derivations (three 'rederive' and two 'skeptic' reports), all in exact rational arithmetic with no floats in any decision path, agree to the last digit on every load-bearing quantity, and a sixth exact Fraction-only recomputation I ran during synthesis (scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-CLTN/083b78b8-b6de-5340-9343-2e5fdd9085d8/scratchpad/wf_verify/synth_check/check.py) reproduces all of them: the fixed point x, det(I-W), the six characteristic-polynomial coefficients of -I+W, and the six Hurwitz minors D1..D6 at both P1 and P2. No report found a real error. Agreement is not just numerical but methodological: stability was decided by (a) exact Hurwitz leading minors (three-valued; no minor is zero, so the case is DECIDED, not boundary), (b) an exact Routh table with zero sign changes, (c) an exact Lyapunov solve (36x36 rational system, residual exactly zero, P symmetric, Sylvester minors all positive), (d) Lienard-Chipart in both odd- and even-minor forms, (e) sympy exact complex-root isolation giving rational upper bounds on max Re(lambda) of -25914987/68719476736 (P1) and -1375204539/35184372088832 (P2), (f) Sturm count of the degree-36 resultant Res(p(lambda), p(s-lambda)) in [0,oo) equal to zero, and (g) shifted-Hurwitz bisection. The fixed-point condition was checked as (I-W)x = 1 with residual exactly zero plus x_i = [Wx+1]_+ exactly with every unit active; condition 2 is vacuous for full support. Legality was checked against the verbatim definitions of both papers (delta>0, 0<eps<delta/(1+delta), equivalently q>1): P1 margin 74/267953, P2 margin 974/26079053. Geneson's two-clause nondegeneracy also holds (63 principal minors + 192 column-replacement determinants nonzero at each point). theta only rescales x, so the verdict is theta-independent. Positive control: the same verifiers flag Geneson's published graph at delta=29eps/25 as POS/STABLE; negative controls: X at q=4 and q=400/101 (inside the proven-safe region) is correctly NOT stable, and the edge-reversed graph is NOT a fixed point. Robustness: the counterexample is not a single point but a one-parameter family; at fixed eps it holds for every legal q in (1, q_hi] with q_hi ~ 1.07230 (eps=1/101, exact degree-5 minimal polynomial) and ~1.08194 (eps=1/1001), the upper end being set by positivity (x_5 -> 0) rather than stability, and the eps->0 limit at delta/eps=27/26 is Hurwitz-stable with margin/eps -> ~-0.0392. This thin window just above q=1 explains why coarse q-sampling (e.g. q=3/2) missed it, consistent with CLAUDE.md section 5.

CONCERNS RAISED AND THEIR STATUS. (1) Convention sensitivity [reports 1,3,4,5]: with the transposed adjacency the spectrum is identical but x has three negative entries, so the claim depends on W[i][j] = -1+eps iff j->i. RESOLVED: report 4 extracted Curto-Morrison eq.(5) and Geneson section 2 verbatim and both match the task convention; report 3 confirmed ctln.py reads A[j][i] and returns bit-identical results; and the only convention error with any effect (transposition) would HIDE this counterexample, not manufacture it. (2) CLAUDE.md section 2 writes the closed form with A_sigma untransposed, whereas under the stated A convention it holds only with A^T [reports 1-5]. RESOLVED for ctln.py (report 3: identity_check_IminusW codes A[sj][si]); UNRESOLVED for symbolic.py, which no report read; this does not affect the present claim, which was verified without repo code. (3) Thin margins (max Re ~ -3.8e-4 at P1, -3.9e-5 at P2; D6 ~ 3e-25 and 4e-40) [all reports]: RESOLVED by exact arithmetic with no zero entries anywhere; report 5 shows the margin is ~3.8-3.9% of eps and converges to ~3.92% eps as eps->0, i.e. structural O(eps), not a boundary coincidence. Any float-based re-check is untrustworthy here and must not be used to second-guess the exact result. (4) Thin q-window [reports 4,5]: not a defect; both reports agree on the endpoints and on positivity failing first. (5) No radical closed forms for eigenvalues [report 1]: not a defect; certified by isolating rectangles, Sturm and bisection, with mutually consistent bounds across reports 1,4,5. (6) Display-only quirks (RealInterval.refine not tightening the upper endpoint; two illegal q<1 rows in a context loop; a mislabelled print in the context report) [reports 1, context]: RESOLVED, none in a decision path. (7) Partial methodological independence of report 3 from ctln.py (same algorithm family): RESOLVED by reports 1, 2 and 5, which use different mathematics (Lyapunov/Sylvester, root isolation, resultant), and by my recomputation. (8) Nondegeneracy formulation [reports 4,5]: OQ10 as stated by Curto-Morrison carries no nondegeneracy clause; Geneson's does; report 4 read Geneson's definition and both clauses hold; RESOLVED. (9) Geneson's N matrix recovered from PDF text with a split row [report 4]: affects only the non-isomorphism side check; the context report independently extracted the same 19-edge G via pdftotext, and the edge count (18 vs 19) alone forces non-isomorphism; RESOLVED for the mathematical claim. (10) Two-parameter symbolic region did not finish [report 4]: UNRESOLVED but out of scope for the pointwise claim; only univariate windows exist. (11) Scope [all reports]: only full support and only P1, P2 were verified, exactly as claimed; nothing is asserted about smaller supports. (12) Literature novelty [context]: X was NOT FOUND in Geneson's paper (one graph, 19 edges) or the ipitchford/ctln-six-is-minimal repo (same graph), but that search relied partly on WebFetch summaries; novelty is likely but less firmly established than the mathematical claim. (13) Process note from synthesis: my own first Faddeev-LeVerrier run was wrong (double-added c_k I) and was caught solely by the check 'constant coefficient == det(I-W)'; after the fix all numbers matched. That identity, plus trace = -6, is the cheapest sanity check a human can run.
